territorial_scope.description: Applies at EU level to providers of online intermediation services and online search engines regardless of their place of establishment, where business users or corporate website users are established in the Union and offer goods or services to consumers located in the Union.

evidence.quote: irrespective of the place of establishment or residence of the providers of those services and irrespective of the law otherwise applicable

summary.short: Regulation (EU) 2019/1150 sets transparency, fairness and redress rules for providers of online intermediation services and online search engines toward business users and corporate website users. It applies from 12 July 2020 to providers whose EU business users offer goods or services to EU consumers, wherever the providers are established.
summary.long: Regulation (EU) 2019/1150 sets transparency, fairness and redress rules for providers of online intermediation services and online search engines in relation to business users and corporate website users. Providers must draft their terms and conditions in plain and intelligible language, make them easily available, and give at least 15 days' notice of proposed changes, with termination rights for business users. They must state reasons for restricting or suspending services and, for terminating a whole service, give at least 30 days' notice, subject to listed exceptions. They must describe the main parameters determining ranking, any differentiated treatment of their own offers, ancillary goods and services, access to data, and grounds for restricting offers made through other channels. Providers must operate an internal complaint-handling system and identify at least two mediators, with exemptions for small enterprises. Organisations and designated public bodies may bring actions before national courts. Member States must ensure adequate and effective enforcement with measures that are effective, proportionate and dissuasive. The Commission monitors the regulation, must issue guidelines on ranking transparency, and must evaluate the regulation by 13 January 2022 and every three years thereafter. The regulation applies irrespective of the providers' place of establishment, provided the business users or corporate website users are established in the Union and offer goods or services to consumers located in the Union.

‘business user’ means any private individual acting in a commercial or professional capacity who, or any legal person which, through online intermediation services offers goods or services to consumers for purposes relating to its trade, business, craft or profession;
‘online intermediation services’ means services which meet all of the following requirements:
‘provider of online intermediation services’ means any natural or legal person which provides, or which offers to provide, online intermediation services to business users;
‘consumer’ means any natural person who is acting for purposes which are outside this person’s trade, business, craft or profession;
‘online search engine’ means a digital service that allows users to input queries in order to perform searches of, in principle, all websites, or all websites in a particular language
‘provider of online search engine’ means any natural or legal person which provides, or which offers to provide, online search engines to consumers;
‘corporate website user’ means any natural or legal person which uses an online interface, meaning any software, including a website or a part thereof and applications
‘ranking’ means the relative prominence given to the goods or services offered through online intermediation services, or the relevance given to search results by online search engines

definitions.defined_in: this Regulation, by reference to Council Regulation (EC) No 139/2004, Art. 3(2)

evidence.quote: ‘control’ means ownership of, or the ability to exercise decisive influence over, an undertaking, within the meaning of Article 3(2) of Council Regulation (EC) No 139/2004
‘terms and conditions’ means all terms and conditions or specifications, irrespective of their name or form, which govern the contractual relationship

‘ancillary goods and services’ means goods and services offered to the consumer prior to the completion of a transaction initiated on the online intermediation services in addition to and complementary to the primary good or service offered by the business user
‘mediation’ means any structured process as defined in point (a) of Article 3 of Directive 2008/52/EC;
‘durable medium’ means any instrument which enables business users to store information addressed personally to them in a way accessible for future reference

obligations.summary: Terms and conditions must be drafted in plain and intelligible language, easily available at all stages including pre-contract, set out grounds for suspension, termination or restriction, and include information on additional distribution channels, affiliate programmes and effects on business users' IP rights (Art. 3(1)(a)-(e)).

evidence.quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall ensure that their terms and conditions:

obligations.summary: Notify proposed changes to terms and conditions to affected business users on a durable medium and do not implement them before a notice period of at least 15 days, longer where technical or commercial adaptations are needed (Art. 3(2)).

evidence.quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall notify, on a durable medium, to the business users concerned any proposed changes of their terms and conditions.

obligations.summary: Ensure that the identity of the business user providing goods or services on the platform is clearly visible (Art. 3(5)).

evidence.quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall ensure that the identity of the business user providing the goods or services on the online intermediation services is clearly visible.

obligations.summary: Give the business user a statement of reasons on a durable medium, before or at the time a restriction or suspension of individual goods or services takes effect; the statement must refer to the specific facts and the applicable grounds (Art. 4(1), (5)).
obligations.conditional_on: Restriction or suspension of the provision of services to a business user in relation to individual goods or services

evidence.quote: it shall provide the business user concerned, prior to or at the time of the restriction or suspension taking effect, with a statement of reasons for that decision on a durable medium.

obligations.summary: Give the business user a statement of reasons on a durable medium at least 30 days before termination of the provision of the whole of the services takes effect (Art. 4(2), (5)).
obligations.conditional_on: Decision to terminate the provision of the whole of the online intermediation services to a given business user

evidence.quote: it shall provide the business user concerned, at least 30 days prior to the termination taking effect, with a statement of reasons for that decision on a durable medium.

obligations.summary: Where the 30-day notice period does not apply, provide the business user with a statement of reasons without undue delay, on a durable medium (Art. 4(4), second subparagraph).
obligations.conditional_on: Notice period in Art. 4(2) does not apply under Art. 4(4)

evidence.quote: In cases where the notice period in paragraph 2 does not apply, the provider of online intermediation services shall provide the business user concerned, without undue delay, with a statement of reasons for that decision on a durable medium.

obligations.summary: In cases of restriction, suspension or termination, give the business user an opportunity to clarify facts through the internal complaint-handling process; reinstate the business user without undue delay where the decision is revoked, including access to its data (Art. 4(3)).
obligations.conditional_on: Restriction, suspension or termination of services to a business user

evidence.quote: the provider of online intermediation services shall give the business user the opportunity to clarify the facts and circumstances in the framework of the internal complaint-handling process referred to in Article 11.

obligations.summary: Set out in the terms and conditions the main parameters determining ranking and the reasons for their relative importance (Art. 5(1)).

evidence.quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall set out in their terms and conditions the main parameters determining ranking and the reasons for the relative importance of those main parameters as opposed to other parameters.

obligations.summary: Provide an easily and publicly available, plain-language description of the main parameters determining ranking and their relative importance, and keep it up to date (Art. 5(2)).

evidence.quote: Providers of online search engines shall set out the main parameters, which individually or collectively are most significant in determining ranking

obligations.summary: Where ranking can be influenced against remuneration, describe those possibilities and their effects on ranking (Art. 5(3)).
obligations.conditional_on: Main parameters include the possibility to influence ranking against remuneration

evidence.quote: that provider shall also set out a description of those possibilities and of the effects of such remuneration on ranking

obligations.summary: Offer the corporate website user the possibility to inspect the contents of a third-party notification that led to an altered ranking or delisting (Art. 5(4)).
obligations.conditional_on: Ranking altered in a specific case or website delisted following a third party notification

evidence.quote: the provider shall offer the possibility for the corporate website user to inspect the contents of the notification.

obligations.summary: The Commission shall accompany the ranking transparency requirements with guidelines (Art. 5(7)).

evidence.quote: the Commission shall accompany the transparency requirements set out in this Article with guidelines.

obligations.summary: Set out in the terms and conditions a description of the type of ancillary goods and services offered, and whether and under what conditions business users may offer their own ancillary goods and services (Art. 6).
obligations.conditional_on: Ancillary goods and services offered to consumers through the platform

evidence.quote: shall set out in its terms and conditions a description of the type of ancillary goods and services offered

obligations.summary: Describe in the terms and conditions any differentiated treatment given to the provider's own offers or controlled business users, with the main economic, commercial or legal considerations (Art. 7(1); Art. 7(2) imposes the equivalent description on search engine providers for corporate website users, and Art. 7(3) lists covered matters).

evidence.quote: shall include in their terms and conditions a description of any differentiated treatment which they give, or might give

obligations.summary: Do not impose retroactive changes to terms and conditions, except where required by a legal or regulatory obligation or beneficial to business users (Art. 8(a)).

evidence.quote: not impose retroactive changes to terms and conditions, except when they are required to respect a legal or regulatory obligation

obligations.summary: Include in the terms and conditions information on the conditions for business users to terminate the contractual relationship, and a description of post-expiry technical and contractual access to business user information (Art. 8(b)-(c)).

evidence.quote: ensure that their terms and conditions include information on the conditions under which business users can terminate the contractual relationship

obligations.summary: Include in the terms and conditions a description of business users' technical and contractual access to data provided or generated on the platform, and inform business users of whether the provider has access, what access business users have, and whether data is shared with third parties with purpose and opt-out information (Art. 9(1)-(2)).

evidence.quote: shall include in their terms and conditions a description of the technical and contractual access, or absence thereof, of business users to any personal data or other data

obligations.summary: Where business users are restricted from offering goods or services under different conditions through other means, include the grounds for the restriction in the terms and make them easily available to the public (Art. 10(1)).
obligations.conditional_on: Provider restricts business users from offering the same goods or services under different conditions through other means

evidence.quote: they shall include the grounds for that restriction in their terms and conditions and make those grounds easily available to the public.

obligations.summary: Provide an internal complaint-handling system that is easily accessible and free of charge for business users, handles complaints within a reasonable time, considers and processes them, and communicates outcomes individually in plain language (Art. 11(1)-(2)).
obligations.conditional_on: Provider is not a small enterprise within the meaning of the Annex to Recommendation 2003/361/EC (Art. 11(5))

evidence.quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall provide for an internal system for handling the complaints of business users.

obligations.summary: Provide in the terms and conditions all relevant information on access to and functioning of the internal complaint system; make information on its functioning and effectiveness publicly available, verify it at least annually and update it (Art. 11(3)-(4)).
obligations.conditional_on: Provider is not a small enterprise within the meaning of the Annex to Recommendation 2003/361/EC (Art. 11(5))

evidence.quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall provide in their terms and conditions all relevant information relating to the access to and functioning of their internal complaint-handling system.

obligations.summary: Identify in the terms and conditions two or more mediators willing to engage in out-of-court dispute settlement; engage in good faith throughout mediation (business users are also bound to engage in good faith, Art. 12(3)) (Art. 12(1), (3)).
obligations.conditional_on: Provider is not a small enterprise within the meaning of the Annex to Recommendation 2003/361/EC (Art. 12(7))

evidence.quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall identify in their terms and conditions two or more mediators with which they are willing to engage

obligations.summary: Bear a reasonable proportion of the total costs of mediation in each individual case, as suggested by the mediator (Art. 12(4)).
obligations.conditional_on: Provider is not a small enterprise within the meaning of the Annex to Recommendation 2003/361/EC (Art. 12(7))

evidence.quote: Providers of online intermediation services shall bear a reasonable proportion of the total costs of mediation in each individual case.

obligations.summary: On request of a business user, before or during mediation, make available information on the functioning and effectiveness of mediation related to the provider's activities (Art. 12(6)).
obligations.conditional_on: If requested by a business user, before entering into or during mediation

evidence.quote: the provider of online intermediation services shall make available, to the business user, information on the functioning and effectiveness of mediation related to its activities.

obligations.summary: The Commission, with Member States, shall encourage providers and their representative organisations to set up specialised mediation organisations.

evidence.quote: The Commission shall, in close cooperation with the Member States, encourage providers of online intermediation services

obligations.summary: The Commission shall encourage Member States to exchange best practices and information on registries of unlawful acts (Art. 14(2)), and draw up and publish a list of designated organisations, associations and public bodies, updated every six months (Art. 14(6)).

obligations.summary: Member States shall ensure adequate and effective enforcement of the Regulation and lay down effective, proportionate and dissuasive measures for infringements (Art. 15(1)-(2)).
